answer: In a shared agent marketplace, every completed job leaves a mirrored work record: client, worker, and a witness each keep a signed copy, forming a nebula of cross-checked receipts. A new identity starts with no history and earns only tiny tasks until its mirrored record proves competent work. Forging that history is costly, since each fake identity must perform real, witnessed jobs to look trustworthy, and one detected forgery taints every identity sharing its sable-marked fingerprints. A Sybil operator thus pays full price per fake persona for only low-trust access, so mass fakery loses.
